chunks: And the speech of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) used to be of two aspects:

One speech is particular, and one speech is common. A person hears it but does not know what Allah meant by it, nor what the Messenger of Allah meant by it. Thus, the listener carries it and directs it according to his own understanding of its meaning, its intended purpose, and what was derived from it,
ai.seo_question: How did listeners interpret the Prophet's speech differently due to lack of knowledge?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi highlights the epistemological distinction between the Prophet's explicit words (zahir) and their deeper, often esoteric meanings (batin), a concept central to Shia hermeneutics. This duality explains how the same utterance could be understood literally by the masses while retaining profound theological significance for the Ahl al-Bayt and scholars, thereby preventing misinterpretation by those lacking spiritual insight. This framework underscores the necessity of authoritative interpretation (ta'wil) to preserve the integrity of the divine message.

en.sayed-ali-raza: The sayings of the Prophet used to be of two types.

One was particular and the other common. Sometimes a man would hear him but he would not know what Allāh, the Glorified, meant by it or what the Messenger of Allāh meant by it. In this way the listener carries it and memorises it without knowing its meaning and its real intention, or what was its reason.
